summary: Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her degrees and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, later serving as professor and dean at the University of Bern, where she became Emerita around 2023.

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indologist and historian. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Jesus College, Oxford (M.A.), and Lincoln's Inn. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at Calcutta University (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India (~1923–1924).

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was an archaeologist and Indologist. He held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and succeeded Rakhal Das Banerji, later serving as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1937 to 1944.

Kashinath Trimbak Telang worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai, where he later served as syndic (1881) and vice-chancellor (1892–1893). He also served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1889–1893).

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1914–1945) and Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1956–1976), teaching students including Masaaki Hattori.

Kate Crosby is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She held the Seiyu Kiriyama post at SOAS, a post at Cardiff University (attested 2002), and is attested as Visiting Professor of Buddhist Studies at King's College London in 2026.
Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London in 2008 and held an attested affiliation at Birkbeck, University of London, in 2010.
Katharina Sabernig is a Tibetologist who earned her PhD at the University of Vienna in 2017. She has held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and archaeology. She completed her doctoral studies under supervisor Gudrun Bühnemann, also receiving instruction from Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at Davidson College and the University of Chicago (PhD), she was supervised by Paul J. Griffiths and taught by William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned an M.A. from the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. from McGill University, where she began serving as professor around 1978.
Katherine R. Tsiang is a scholar of archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She is affiliated with the University of Chicago, with faculty posts attested in 2012 and 2026.

Kathleen D. Morrison is a scholar of archaeology and Indology. Educated at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley, she served as Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Northwestern (~1993–1995) and joined the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

Kathleen Kenyon was an archaeologist educated at St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College. She held positions at the University of London (~1935–1962), the UCL Institute of Archaeology (1948–1962), and St Hugh's College, Oxford (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, DePauw University, Lewis & Clark College (1987–1993), and Florida State University as Associate Professor of Religion (~1993–2017).

Kathrin Holz specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg, where she was taught by Ingo Strauch, and has held a research affiliation with the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
Kathryn H. Selig Brown works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned her PhD in 2000 from the University of Michigan, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Walter M. Spink.

Katia Buffetrille is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under Alexander W. Macdonald at Paris Nanterre University (PhD 1996) and held posts at the EPHE (~1996), CRCAO, and as an editor of EMSCAT.

Katragadda Paddayya is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his doctorate from Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1964–1968). He spent his career at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1970–2008), including as Professor of Geo-archaeology (~1995–2008).
